description.p: Jot is a Markdown notes app for Linux. Notes are plain files in a folder you choose, and sync is optional: none, a folder another tool already syncs, S3, Dropbox or Google Drive.
Jot is at an early stage. It shares its look and its themes with Callie, the calendar from the same makers.

ul.li: Jot has its own website, jotwriter.org, and its installer moved there: curl -fsSL https://jotwriter.org/install.sh | sh. The old addresses on callieapp.org keep working.
Jot's code, issues and releases moved to github.com/greylocklabs/jot. The About dialog, problem reports and jot upgrade use the new addresses.
Settings, Theme, Note text: write notes in the theme's font, a serif or a mono one.
Code blocks take their colors from the theme, worked out from its accent, so they match it. A theme file can set them, and the note font, in a new [editor] section.

Notebooks can be made, renamed and moved without a file manager: the + beside Notebooks makes one, a double-click renames one, and dragging a note or a notebook onto another moves it there. Links to the notes inside keep working.

Right-click a note for Open, Rename, Move to, Copy link, Show in Files, Make a task and Move to trash, or a notebook for a new note or notebook inside it, Rename and Show in Files. The Menu key opens the selected note's.
The sidebar and the note list can be made wider or narrower by dragging their edges; a double-click puts one back. While a note or notebook is dragged, a copy of it follows the pointer.
The format row's Formatted and Source buttons switch between styled and as-written Markdown, its Task switch makes the note a task, and its H button holds the three heading sizes. Done is a checkbox.
Delete moves the selected note, or the notebook clicked in the sidebar, to the trash after asking; a notebook's menu offers the same. A notebook goes with everything in it.

Vi mode, under Settings, Keyboard. Notes open in normal mode, where h, j, k and l move, x, dd and p edit and u undoes; i, a or o start typing and Esc stops, and v selects. Out of a note, j and k go through the list, and / searches it: Enter goes to what was found, Esc clears the search and leaves it. A leader key, comma by default, starts commands such as a new note or the tasks, and shows what can follow it if the next key is slow to come.
The keyboard shortcuts list (F1) is made from the same table as the shortcuts themselves, vi mode's keys included.
To-dos are now tasks, everywhere: the sidebar's Tasks, the Task button, and jot tasks. A note that is a task says task: open or task: done in its front matter; todo: is no longer read.
The keyboard shortcuts dialog shows again.
The fold arrow beside a notebook comes to a clean point.
A long note opens at its title, not scrolled part way down.
The sidebar leaves room under the title bar.
jot upgrade on a computer without Jot's package names Jot's installer, not Callie's.

Lists carry on as you type: Return starts the next bullet, number or unticked box, Return on an empty item ends the list, and Tab and Shift+Tab nest and unnest items. Shift+Return breaks the line without a new item.

Tables: the format bar's table button adds one, or lines up the one you are in. Tab and Shift+Tab move between cells, padding them so the columns align; Tab in the last cell and Return add a row, and Return on an empty last row ends the table. Tables show in a monospace font so the columns line up on screen too.

Typing [[ offers your notes as you go, by title, alias or folder. Arrows choose one, Return or Tab puts it in and closes the link, and Escape puts the list away. When two notes share a title, the link names its folder too.
Ctrl+/ or the Source button shows a note's Markdown exactly as written, in the monospace font, with nothing folded away; again brings the styling back. Jot remembers which you prefer.
Code blocks are colored by their language, named after the opening fence ( python , rust , sh and hundreds more), through KDE's syntax highlighting.

Open a folder of Markdown notes as your vault. The sidebar lists its notebooks, which fold, and its tags; the middle column lists their notes, newest or by title, and searches them; Ctrl+P finds any note by a few letters of its title, an alias or its folder.

Write notes in Markdown that styles itself as you type: headings grow, and the marks behind emphasis, links and code fold away except on the line you are on. Notes save as you type. Ctrl+N makes a note, its title renames it and every link to it, Ctrl+click follows a link (or makes the note a wikilink names), and a click ticks a task.
Paste an image, or drop files on a note, to keep them beside it in its .assets folder. An image on a line of its own shows in place of its link.
Under each note, the lines that link to it, and the notes that name it without a link. Resting the pointer on a link shows the start of the note it leads to.
To-dos, in the sidebar: notes that are to-dos, soonest due first, and every unticked box in the vault. Ticking one changes its note; choosing one opens the note on that line.
jot status, ls, search, new, show, open and todo work on your vault from a terminal, with --json for scripts; jot new takes a note's body from a pipe.

A row of formatting over each note: headings, bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links, lists, checkboxes, quotes and code blocks, each also undone in one step, and most with a shortcut. The To-do button makes the note a to-do, with a due date and a Done switch under its title.

Settings, under the title bar's slider button or Ctrl+,: change the notes folder, pick, import, export or recolor a theme, and turn off the daily check for new releases. The ? menu copies debug info, reports a bug, lists the keyboard shortcuts, says what is new, and tells you when an update is out.
jot upgrade and jot downgrade install another release, jot logs and jot doctor help with bug reports, and the jot command completes in bash, zsh and fish.
Add an install script
A first window with Callie's look: the shared themes, a rounded frame and its own title bar.
.deb and .rpm packages for Fedora, Debian and Ubuntu.
